newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sets up new labour coordination body.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sets up new labour coordination body.

text.p: Hungary has set aside 119 billion forints in 1997 for job creation and unemployment support, officials said on Thursday.
The funds will be overseen by a new body, the Labour Fund Coordination Council (MAT) made up of government representatives, employers and unions, Labour Minister Peter Kiss told a news conference.
"Our labour policy does not suffer from a shortage of funds but we do have to set the right priorities," he said.
Unemployment in Hungary was 10.5 percent, or 477,500, in December and the rate was expected to remain unchanged for the first half of this year.
Kiss added that keeping the existing number of jobs and possibly supplementing them is the top priority.
"Now that the shrinking of jobs has stopped, we can concentrate on maintaining existing workplaces and creating new ones," he said. @

He acknowledged that there are considerable differences between the country's regions in terms of unemployment and added that regional bodies are independent enough to deal with the most urgent tasks.
"Crisis and conflict management is becoming less of a central problem," Kiss said.
The new body, has 18 members, spread equally between government representatives, employers and employees.
